label: History
value: Mrs. Sowerby spent many years residing on her family farm in Brierley
unit: Mrs. Sowerby spent many years residing on her family farm in Brierley with her husband, Thomas Sowerby. She frequently visited Grey Shutters and dropped by neighbors' homes to discuss local matters or solicit contributions for parish needs. When Nell Harcourt first arrived at Grey Shutters as a child, Mrs. Sowerby openly commented on her thin frame and freckles, sparking a violent outburst of rage from Nell and causing a brief strain in her visits. In later years, she cared untiringly for her husband throughout his prolonged illness until his silent passing. Facing financial hardship and the necessity of selling her farm after Thomas's death, she felt heartbroken at the prospect of leaving Brierley until Thirza Abernethy invited her to move into Grey Shutters.

label: History
value: Anthony attended the Brierley School.
unit: Anthony attended the Brierley School in the class taught by Nell Harcourt. On the first day of the school term, he sat alone in a corner desk and glared at his new teacher with open enmity. During recess on his first day, he emptied water from his slate bottle down the back of Aurelia Clay's neck, after which Nell kept him inside to lecture him on how gentlemen should behave toward ladies, though he left unaffected with a contemptuous whistle. Months later, during winter, his behavior led Nell to snap and strike him across his hand with a hardwood pointer until tears filled his eyes. Rather than harboring a permanent grudge, Anthony's respect was won by the beating; he subsequently tipped his cap to Nell, carried her school books through deep snow, and remarked that her thrashing was as good as a man's.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia's only daughter got married
unit: After her only daughter got married and departed for foreign missionary work, Aunt Euphemia was left living alone in a large house. To alleviate her loneliness, she agreed to move to Portmaris and act as the housekeeper for her niece Mabel Colby and her friends, Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis, at Tabby's Place. Upon her arrival, she brought along two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and quickly settled into the household. She offered warmth, conversation, and gentle guidance to the young women living with her while resisting urges to strictly regulate their behavior.

Too bashful to ask her himself, he repeatedly harassed his sister Odette until she agreed to propose to Nell on his behalf. Through Odette, he offered to marry Nell before spring planting or wait until her college education was finished, but Nell firmly rejected the proposal.

label: History
value: Leonora Bowman went to reside at Echo Cottage.
unit: Following the precedent set by her three elder sisters, Leonora Bowman went to reside at Echo Cottage with Miss Rosalind Penrose to assist with household duties in exchange for garments, board, and room. Because of her strong resemblance to her sisters, Miss Rosalind dubbed her "Belinda the Fourth." Unlike her older sisters, Belinda never openly criticized Miss Rosalind's imaginative pretend games. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke accidentally arrived at Echo Cottage while seeking directions, Belinda assisted in serving tea and demonstrated the cottage's famous forest echoes by blowing a small tin horn and laughing loudly for the guests. She developed a profound admiration for Nell, frequently practicing in her bedroom mirror to imitate Nell's posture and movements. During a later summer, Belinda invited Nell to gather early strawberries in Mr. Kimball's pasture, where she confided her grave worries regarding Miss Rosalind's declining health and strange behavior.

unit: Following the precedent set by her three elder sisters, Leonora Bowman went to reside at Echo Cottage with Miss Rosalind Penrose to assist with household duties in exchange for garments, board, and room. Because of her strong resemblance to her sisters, Miss Rosalind dubbed her "Belinda the Fourth." Unlike her older sisters, Belinda never openly criticized Miss Rosalind's imaginative pretend games. When Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke accidentally arrived at Echo Cottage while seeking directions, Belinda assisted in serving tea and demonstrated the cottage's famous forest echoes by blowing a small tin horn and laughing loudly for the guests. She developed a profound admiration for Nell, frequently practicing in her bedroom mirror to imitate Nell's posture and movements. During a later summer, Belinda invited Nell to gather early strawberries in Mr. Kimball's pasture, where she confided her grave worries regarding Miss Rosalind's declining health and strange behavior.

label: History
value: Cedric moved from Boston
unit: Cedric moved from Boston to live with his grandmother on the shore road in Brierley. At school, he became a beloved student of Nell Harcourt, who appreciated his rich imagination and unique personality. He shared letters with Nell detailing his imaginary stone companions by the beach, such as Nora, the Twin Sailors, and the Golden Lady. He also engaged in a friendly fight with St. Clair Trask regarding their respective national flags. Nell brought Cedric to visit Miss Rosalind Penrose at her stone house, where Cedric quickly bonded with her over shared fancies of dream-people. When his father, Stephen Stanhope, unexpectedly arrived in town, Cedric warmly introduced him to Nell, ultimately helping to rekindle the relationship between his father and Miss Rosalind.

label: History
value: Flossie attended Brierley school.
unit: Flossie attended Brierley school under Miss Thorne, where she openly expressed her dislike for recitation afternoons. At the conclusion of one school session, she directly questioned Miss Thorne about whether she would be returning the following year. She later traveled alongside classmates to take the entrance examinations at the Academy, where she remarked to Nell Harcourt about her pale appearance and warned her about the bad luck of being assigned number thirteen. After entering Regent's, she became known as the most caustic-tongued student in her class. Later, Flossie and her family hosted a send-off celebration for Nell and Hugh Carrow organized by the B.V.I.S., during which she behaved politely and offered a patronizing compliment to Nell on her new dress.

label: History
value: Honora Hollis attended Regent's Academy
unit: Honora Hollis attended Regent's Academy with Nell Harcourt. She was later assigned as the schoolteacher in Delford. During her time teaching, she drove out to visit Nell Harcourt at Grey Shutters alongside her aunt, Mrs. Charlotte E. Varley, and Mrs. Pendexter. Later, she enrolled as a student at Wexcombe College alongside Nell, where both girls became deeply involved in classes, social activities, and the Freshmen class spirit. While visiting Old St. John's cemetery at Wexcombe, Honora and Nell struck up an immediate friendship with Cressida Lindsay, who introduced them into wider social circles. Honora also consulted with Nell over Mabel Colby's proposal to lease a small home together in Portmaris with Mabel's Aunt Euphemia.

label: History
value: Hugh attended Brierley School.
unit: Hugh attended Brierley School, where he famously pulled Nell Harcourt's crimson plait and teased her, prompting her to break her slate over his head. Though he stepped up to take the blame for the incident, Nell refused to forgive him at the time. Over the years, he developed high principles and a strong attachment to Nell, striving to guard his behavior to be worthy of her companionship. After moving on to higher education at Wexcombe College, he led the Freshmen to victory against the Sophomores in the Arts Rush using clever tactics and was subsequently elected president of the Freshman Class. He was also invited to join the Lamba Theta fraternity ("the Lambs"), undergoing their initiation ritual with good humor. During an early spring evening, he met Nell and offered her Mayflowers, ultimately confessing his love and asking her to marry him. Upon being rejected, he was deeply heartbroken and declared that he could not be satisfied with mere friendship before taking his leave to start a new position at the Daily News.

Over the years, he developed high principles and a strong attachment to Nell, striving to guard his behavior to be worthy of her companionship. After moving on to higher education at Wexcombe College, he led the Freshmen to victory against the Sophomores in the Arts Rush using clever tactics and was subsequently elected president of the Freshman Class. He was also invited to join the Lamba Theta fraternity ("the Lambs"), undergoing their initiation ritual with good humor. During an early spring evening, he met Nell and offered her Mayflowers, ultimately confessing his love and asking her to marry him. Upon being rejected, he was deeply heartbroken and declared that he could not be satisfied with mere friendship before taking his leave to start a new position at the Daily News.

label: History
value: Isolde grew up at Pear Hill.
unit: Isolde grew up at Pear Hill beside Pembroke's pond and formed a close, imaginative childhood friendship with Nell Harcourt. Together with Nell, she created a candle-and-cardboard signaling method between their windows. During one nighttime prank, Isolde and Nell jumped onto a bed occupied by a visiting Miss Pembroke, which initially sparked anger but ultimately led to a warm friendship between the older visitor and the girls. While attending school under Miss Thorne, Isolde participated in Friday recitations and outperformed Nell in geometry. As she grew older, Isolde attended Regent's Academy alongside friends like Nell, Opal, and Odette. Later, she served as a confidante for Nell, discussing romantic prospects and mutual acquaintances, and eventually planned her upcoming wedding where Hugh Carrow would serve as best man.

During one nighttime prank, Isolde and Nell jumped onto a bed occupied by a visiting Miss Pembroke, which initially sparked anger but ultimately led to a warm friendship between the older visitor and the girls. While attending school under Miss Thorne, Isolde participated in Friday recitations and outperformed Nell in geometry. As she grew older, Isolde attended Regent's Academy alongside friends like Nell, Opal, and Odette. Later, she served as a confidante for Nell, discussing romantic prospects and mutual acquaintances, and eventually planned her upcoming wedding where Hugh Carrow would serve as best man.

unit: Following the death of her mother, Mary Farrow, Lucy and her twin brother, Robin, were brought to live at Grey Shutters under the care of Thirza Abernethy and Nell Harcourt. She settled into the household routines, helping with chores, attending Sunday School, and tending a garden plot. Lucy commenced her early schooling at Brierley School alongside her brother, where she was provisionally seated next to Mirabel Cotton. Mirabel thoroughly frightened Lucy by recounting detailed stories of deceased relatives and a ghost uncle who roamed the house after burial, causing Lucy to weep in fear of going upstairs alone in the dark until Nell comforted her. Nell subsequently stepped in to stop Mirabel from continuing to tell her frightening family ghost stories.

label: History
value: Mabel studied at Regent's Academy
unit: Mabel studied at Regent's Academy, where she formed a close friendship with Nell Harcourt and Honora Hollis and was recognized as the beauty of the Second Year class. After completing her third year at Regent's, she spent two years teaching at an isolated rural schoolhouse with nine grades, dealing with demanding parents and scholars ranging from four to twenty years old. Weary of country teaching and living in boardings, she wrote to Nell proposing that she, Nell, and Honora pool their resources to lease a furnished house in Portmaris for their upcoming studies at Wexcombe College. She arranged for her lonely aunt, Aunt Euphemia, to move to Portmaris and serve as their housekeeper. Later, while sharing the house, Mabel lived alongside her friends and their pets, despairing over the frequent fighting between her cat Smudge and Aunt Euphemia's cat Joseph.

label: History
value: Nell insists her name be spelled with an E
unit: After being taken in as a child by Thirza and Obed Abernethy at Grey Shutters, Nell insisted that her name be spelled 'with an E' and swore eternal friendship with her neighbor Isolde Pembroke. During her school years, she participated in local rehearsals and concerts while enduring simple attire provided by Thirza. Desperate to get rid of her red hair, she purchased hair dye from an itinerant merchant, which disastrously turned her hair green. Obed later bought her a new dress to match her peers, and on another occasion, she had to rise to the situation and greet unexpected visitors while covered in feathers after transferring a feather bed. At seventeen, she left the Island with Hugh Carrow to pursue her education at Wexcombe in Portmaris, staying with the Harvey sisters alongside Honora Hollis. She subsequently took up a position as a schoolteacher at Coombe Road, lodging with Miss Thora Sweet at 'Wayside.' Soon after, she achieved literary success by selling a story sketch to 'The Youth's Friend' for ten dollars.

label: History
value: Obed traveled to the Alder River station
unit: Obed traveled to the Alder River station expecting to collect a boy from an orphan asylum brought by Mrs. Alexander Tranter. Upon arriving, he was astonished to discover that a girl, young Nell Harcourt, had been left for him instead. Unable to bring himself to turn her away, he brought her to Grey Shutters to let his sister Thirza manage the situation. After learning that the alternative for Nell was being taken in by Mrs. Scobie, Obed advocated for keeping her, declaring he would not give a dog he cared for to Mrs. Scobie. Sometime later, wanting to buy Nell a gift, he nervously entered an unfamiliar store to buy dress fabric, became thoroughly flustered, and ended up purchasing an unwanted garden rake and twenty pounds of brown sugar. He subsequently sought the advice of Mrs. Sowerby, who agreed to purchase suitable material and make a modern dress for Nell on his behalf.

Unable to bring himself to turn her away, he brought her to Grey Shutters to let his sister Thirza manage the situation. After learning that the alternative for Nell was being taken in by Mrs. Scobie, Obed advocated for keeping her, declaring he would not give a dog he cared for to Mrs. Scobie. Sometime later, wanting to buy Nell a gift, he nervously entered an unfamiliar store to buy dress fabric, became thoroughly flustered, and ended up purchasing an unwanted garden rake and twenty pounds of brown sugar. He subsequently sought the advice of Mrs. Sowerby, who agreed to purchase suitable material and make a modern dress for Nell on his behalf.

label: History
value: Odette grew up in Brierley.
unit: Odette grew up in Brierley as part of a close group of four friends that included Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Opal Pettigrew. She attended Regent's class alongside her peers to prepare for teaching credentials. Upon finishing her preparation, she took a teaching position in Stonebridge. She later stepped in to help her bashful brother Barney propose marriage to Nell, though Nell declined. After returning from the West, Odette became engaged to Mr. Inglis, a wealthy mining businessman from Winnipeg forty years her senior. At the end of May, she married Mr. Inglis in a grand wedding before embarking on a European honeymoon and settling into a mansion in Winnipeg.

unit: Opal had a merry, cheerful, and lighthearted disposition, often engrossed in social life, bright clothing, and talk of her suitors. Facing her terminal illness, she harbored a deep fear of death and the unfamiliarity of the afterlife, longing earnestly to live a normal life with love and a family.

label: History
value: During her youth in Brierley, Opal spent midsummer afternoons playing outdoor games.
unit: During her youth in Brierley, Opal spent midsummer afternoons playing outdoor games with Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen around the local pond. She later took up a teaching position at Pale Sands school, though her declining health forced her to step down before completing her term. As her illness worsened, she spent her final summer resting in her garden, frequently seeking the companionship of Nell, in whom she eventually confided her fear of death and her unfulfilled wish to marry Herb Tranter and raise a family. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter and was buried in the local graveyard near her family home, leaving an unfinished piece of embroidery to Nell.

label: Personality
value: Mr. Pettifer is regarded locally as an eccentric.
unit: Regarded locally as an eccentric and stingy crank, Mr. Pettifer is quick-tempered and hasty, yet can be polite, anxious, and gentle once his initial anger passes. He is fiercely independent, maintaining his own home and declaring that he wants no women near his premises. He lacks fixed domestic routines, washing dishes only on rainy Sundays inside a rainwater hogshead and eating only when struck by hunger.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer purchased Robert Bell's farm.
unit: After purchasing Robert Bell's farm to become the western neighbor of Grey Shutters, Mr. Pettifer quickly earned a reputation in Brierley as a stingy eccentric who washed dishes in rain hogsheads and refused to pay minister earnings or mission donations. He hired young John Henry Carter of Pale Sands as his farmhand. When Nell Harcourt mistakenly sold his strayed Jersey cow to a passing dealer, Mr. Pettifer admitted he had acted too hastily previously and gently pardoned her, despite his foul-mouthed parrot Nutmeg repeatedly insulting her. He later employed a clumsy new worker whom he described as having left-handed traits in both feet. When Nell considered writing a fiction story, she confided in Mr. Pettifer, who discouraged her by remarking that too much rubbish was already being published.

label: History
value: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley School.
unit: Mr. Pidgeon served as the schoolmaster at Brierley School, lodging at the residence of Eben Duckett during his tenure. While teaching, he spent considerable effort instructing older pupils in subjects such as algebra and preparing them for Regent's entrance examinations while largely neglecting the younger children. During one afternoon, after returning from dinner to find several students late, he sought a victim to enforce discipline and singled out Nell Harcourt. He forced her to sit next to Hugh Carrow as a punishment and made her stand at the front of the room under a humiliating message written on the blackboard. Following this incident, Nell refused to return to his classroom for a period. Local community members, including Mrs. Agatha Sowerby, criticized his ineffective teaching and poor classroom management, noting that he only retained his teaching position because his uncle was a primary school trustee.

label: History
value: Ezra studied theology at St. Columbia
unit: Ezra studied theology at St. Columbia after graduating from Wexcombe. During one summer, he took charge of the Prospect Point Mission Church, where he stayed at a local boardinghouse. There, he formed a swift friendship with Cressida Lindsay, accompanying her on fishing, boating, and moonlight walking outings. Although he initially resisted entering the ministry, he embraced it as his divine calling and delivered a splendid sermon at the local village church that deeply moved Cressy. The two fell in love and became engaged, planning to marry a year from the following June, after which he would take charge of a small mission church in the slum district on Tanner Street.

value: Robin is spirited.

label: History
value: Robin resides at Grey Shutters.
unit: Robin came to reside at Grey Shutters alongside his twin sister Lucy, where he was cared for by Thirza Abernethy and Nell Harcourt. He frequently disrupted mealtime conversations with misbehavior, such as stretching across the table, bumping Lucy's arm, and licking his plate. Upon learning that his father had passed away, leaving a trust fund for him and Lucy, he was overjoyed to learn that Grey Shutters would remain his permanent home. After starting school, his involvement in domestic trouble decreased. On one occasion, out of jealousy over Nell's affection for Cedric Stanhope, Robin initially refused to say his bedtime prayers, though Nell persuaded him to do so. He also admitted to giving his sister the larger piece of jam-spread bread, taking pride in his improved behavior. On another occasion, after engaging in bad behavior on a Sunday, Robin suffered from a guilty conscience and confessed his remorse to Nell, who comforted him and guided him through a simple prayer. Later, he sold his pulled front tooth to Milty Gammon for two cents and announced his intention to eventually marry his classmate Mabel Fletcher.

label: History
value: Rosalind Penrose grew up as the daughter of old Mr. Penrose
unit: Rosalind Penrose grew up as the daughter of old Mr. Penrose, who built an ancient stone house in an isolated area near West Welby. In her youth, she was considered a notable beauty and became engaged to Stephen Stanhope twenty-five years ago. Following a disagreement, their engagement ended, and Stephen left for the United States. Rosalind withdrew to her quiet stone residence, living largely secluded from social life. Years later, Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke stopped by her home while seeking directions, discovering her pretending to host a tea party with her handmaiden, Belinda the Fourth. Rosalind welcomed them warmly into her home, sharing her imaginative disposition with Nell. Later, Nell brought Stephen's young son, Cedric Stanhope, to visit Echo Cottage, where Rosalind bonded with Cedric over their shared love of imaginary companions and dream-people.

label: History
value: Thirza resided at Grey Shutters
unit: Thirza resided at Grey Shutters with her brother Obed Abernethy when they arranged for a child to be brought to them from an asylum. Expecting a boy, she was surprised when Nell Harcourt arrived instead. Despite the mistake, Thirza and Obed agreed to retain Nell, with Thirza supervising her daily tasks and enforcing strict domestic discipline while sending her to school. When Mrs. Agatha Sowerby harshly insulted Nell's appearance, Thirza punished Nell for her explosive outburst but unexpectedly stood up to Agatha, telling her she had been overly harsh. Thirza later agreed to let Nell attend the local Debating Club concert after Obed persistently advocated for her. When Robin Farrow accidentally ruined the lemon pies prepared for visitors by stepping on them against orders, Thirza strictly sent him to his room for his disobedience.

label: History
value: Miss Thorne served as an educator
unit: Miss Thorne served as a female educator at Brierley School. During her tenure, she conducted bi-weekly recitations, led field trips to the forest to observe nature, and ran daily physical culture routines, though her methods drew criticism from Mrs. Sowerby. At the end of June, her reign as teacher in Brierley came to an end. Her moving departure speech left students like Nell and Isolde tearful and solemn. Prior to the Academy entrance exams, she extracted a promise from her students to refrain from cramming and focus on resting and walking instead. On the morning of the exams, she picked up Nell and drove her to the Academy, stopping along the way to collect pupils Odette, Opal, and Flossie.
